raw_response:
I will still start from what paid me last year, then adjust a little where I think I can get more grain without spending foolishly. I have 340.1 mu, so I cannot manage it like a tiny household plot. I need a simple plan I can repeat across big blocks. In Quzhou, wheat-maize is still the safest money for me because I have well irrigation, the buyers are easy to find, and I have already done it for 3 years. So I will keep most land in wheat followed by maize, and I will leave smaller blocks for soybean and oilseed so I do not put everything into one basket. I finished middle school, so I do look at input cost, water, and yield together, but I do not like gambling on low fertilizer. If I am unsure, I will stay close to what local growers do and keep fertilizer a little on the safe side. For wheat, I will feed it steadily because winter wheat in my area punishes you if base fertilizer is weak. For maize, I will push nitrogen harder because it responds fast after the wheat harvest, but I will keep phosphorus and potassium there so the stalk stays strong and the ear fills. Soybean I will not feed like maize, because too much nitrogen gives me too much vine and not enough pod. Oilseed I will manage more carefully on phosphorus and potassium because that crop needs good rooting and seed filling. Water I will use where it matters most: wheat before winter and at jointing or grain fill, maize at seedling and tasseling if rain is short, soybean and oilseed only when I see they truly need it. On pests, I will not spray blindly, but on a farm this size I will not wait too long either. Missing the right time costs more than one extra pass.
